unit.rule: one attempt = one pair episode (both robots, one seed, one bin). Every count N/S/A/E below is in pair episodes, never robot rows or streams. A pair episode contributes two robot streams to the tensors only when admitted.

world.complete: behavior: judged; in the denominator N (includes end_reason cap_end, planning_wall_safety_cap and teacher_terminal mission failures)
world.HOST_ERROR: environment: excluded from N, counted in E.host_error, seed consumed, re-queued once (same seed, same bin)
world.running: environment: as HOST_ERROR (result.json written before the final update)
world.missing: environment: world absent from summary.worlds or no raw result.json; as HOST_ERROR

batch.clean: summary.status == complete AND summary.HOST_ERROR == 0 AND episode command exit code == 0 (exit-try-<n>.json present) AND summary.rejection_table is an absolute path to an existing file
batch.admission_rejected: environment: every un-ingested slot -> E.admission_error, seed consumed, NOT re-queued (the case is deterministic)
batch.HOST_ERROR_or_exit_nonzero_or_unknown_ex: unclean: worlds present in summary.worlds are judged (behavior, in N and S) but NEVER admitted (audit 1); worlds missing -> environment host_error
batch.interrupted_twice: after MAX_TRIES=2 tries without a final summary the remaining slots are environment host_error (closed as unclean)
batch.validation_unclean: v4: in a validation batch the judged worlds of an unclean batch are environment (unclean_batch_requeue) and re-queued once (seeds.validation.rule); train batches keep audit 1

result_after_grasp: carry (dict with outcome and events list)
carry_eval (dict with success bool, failure, drop_events list, robot_robot_contact_ticks int)
required_fields.summary_world: v5: result carry_eval.success is the single truth. A summary world that has carry_success must equal it (else record_error); a summary world without the key (the gcp6 wrapper before v5: 25 record_error in the gcp2 shard smoke 2026-10-21) is judged from carry_eval.success. A record_error is never S or A
required_fields.missing_or_wrong_type: record_error: the attempt is neither success nor failure, it is rejected; STOP_RECORD stops collection after that batch (no defaults such as 0 drops or physical_success fallback)

success.physical_success_S: world status complete AND grasp_physical_success is true AND carry_eval.success is true AND carry_eval.drop_events == [] AND carry_eval.robot_robot_contact_ticks == 0 (P2 evaluator harness/pair_carry_eval.evaluate unchanged)
success.truth_scope: GT is read only by the eval-only evaluator after the episode; never by the teacher controller or student inputs

filter.admitted_A: S AND search_handoff == false AND approach_handoff == false AND batch clean AND (training) data_admitted == true AND (training) both robot streams pass the stage sidecar check
filter.sidecar_check: per robot r1/r2: teacher-<rid>.jsonl(.zst) and student-<rid>.jsonl(.zst) exist, every teacher row has sample_id and a teacher_phase mapped by harness.pairact_r1.TEACHER_PHASE_TO_STAGE, teacher sample_id set == student sample_id set, >= 1 row. Run at ingest, before the attempt row is written; eligible/admitted is counted only after both robots pass
filter.measurement_mode: no recording -> no sidecar; A in pilot is 'admission candidate' (S AND no handoff AND batch clean) and is labelled '수율 측정, 시연 아님'
filter.success_not_admitted: S but not A: counted in S, tagged success_not_admitted:<reasons> (handoff, batch_not_clean, recording_not_admitted, sidecar_failed), never in tensors
filter.failures: never enter tensors; raw outputs are kept untouched in the batch directories and listed in the ledger with failure stage and carry sub-reason
filter.no_relabel: the filter is a pure function of result.json / summary.json / stream fields named above; no manual selection, no re-judging after viewing videos

carry_outcome (teacher carry.outcome as written, e.g. route_blocked, door_pass_timeout, carry_total_timeout, command_sequence_complete)
carry_fail (last carry.events entry with event == fail: code, phase, detail)

bins.unit: pair episode; both robots of one attempt are drawn inside the same bin (not independent robot-level uniform draws)
bins.distance: planar distance from the robot spawn to the grasp point of its assigned beam end (start_layers.<rid>.target_distance_m)
bins.yaw: own heading offset relative to the assigned-end outward direction (wide_start convention). facing: wrapped offset within 90 deg of pi (robot looks at its end); away: otherwise
bins.roles: r1 end = teal if random.Random('pairact_r1_collect_v1:<seed>:role').random() < 0.5 else blue (not seed parity, which would tie roles to round-robin bins)
bins.position_bearing: radially outward from the assigned end (wide_start bearing bin 0), unchanged from the r13 wide gate
bins.draw_within_bin: per robot: distance uniform in the bin range, yaw offset uniform in the bin half-circle, rng = random.Random('pairact_r1_collect_v1:<seed>:<bin id>:<robot index>') (str seed, sha512, independent of PYTHONHASHSEED) [setup only]

bin_limit.rule: at a batch boundary, a bin with N_b >= 20 attempts and A_b / N_b < 0.20 (admitted rate: the same quantity A_b as the allocation and the stop rules) gets a ledger row bin_limited and receives no further new attempts (re-queues of its own HOST_ERROR seeds still run). It is reported as '구간 범위 제한' with its N_b, S_b, A_b, S_b / N_b (physical success rate, reporting only) and failure sub-reasons. Closing is permanent for the run root
bin_limit.quantity: v4 (xreview R1): v3s retired bins on S_b / N_b while the allocation weighted A_b, so a bin with physical successes that are never admitted (e.g. handoff) kept the deficit weight 20 / p_floor and took most of every batch. Both rules now read A_b; S_b / N_b is reported only
bin_limit.rationale: at 20 attempts and < 20% success the expected attempts to reach 20 admitted exceed 100 (~1/6 of the cap) for one bin; spending them would starve the other bins. 20 attempts keeps the binomial 95% upper bound of a 3/20 admitted rate (~0.38) below the 33% yield the cap of 600 assumes

targets.not_a_denominator: 200 is the admitted target and a stop condition, never a denominator. Reports use S/N and A/N (N = behavior attempts) and validation S/20, A/20
targets.attempt_definition: N counts behavior attempts only (status table). Environment failures consume their seed but are not attempts
targets.overshoot: a batch that crosses 200 runs to its end; every admitted episode of that batch is kept (no trimming, trimming would be a selection)
targets.rationale: 200 = TRAIN200 of solo ACT R8 and close to beamact2's 185 successful pairs; 150 = 75% of it, the smallest set the success-filter decision accepts; 600 = 200 / 0.33 assumed yield (decision doc 3); 20 per bin x 6 = 120 < 150, so the per-bin minimum and the total minimum are separate AND conditions; 80 = training floor (owner 2026-10-21, fixed before any result): below it no training, back to P2
targets.replaces_decision_doc: the decision document's '진행 가능한 최소치 150' (pairact-success-filter-decision.md section 3) is replaced by the four training_decision tiers; 150 now separates TRAIN* from TRAIN_SMALL_DATA and 80 is the no-training floor

stop_rules.order: evaluated at every batch boundary in this order; the first true rule stops train collection
list: STOP_RECORD: any record_error attempt (missing/ill-typed required field, unregistered status, summary/result carry disagreement)

STOP_HOST: two consecutive finished train batches (batch order) are both unclean (status table batch; in a serial run these are the last two at the boundary where it first holds, and later batches cannot undo it), OR some shard meets stop_rules.shard_host (K = 1: the whole run is one shard)

STOP_DISTANCE: A >= 150 AND every far bin (B4, B5) has A_b >= 20 or is bin_limited (owner decision D-v4-1) AND the distance gate fails on the current admitted set (checked at every boundary from then on)
STOP_TARGET: A >= 200 and every bin has A_b >= 20 or is bin_limited
STOP_SEEDS: every train seed (8340000-8340599) is consumed and no train re-queue is pending
stop_rules.seed_consumption_note: environment failures consume seeds without adding to N, so STOP_SEEDS can occur with N < 600 (e.g. 600 seeds / 599 attempts after one final HOST_ERROR). STOP_SEEDS is treated exactly like STOP_CAP; there is no seed range beyond 8340599 and no replacement seed

shard_host.rule: per shard i (train batches k with k % K == i in batch order, K = header shard count, 1 for a serial run): 3 unclean finished batches in a row, OR a prefix of at least 6 finished batches with >= 30% unclean -> STOP_HOST (decision.host_stop names the shard). Both are prefix properties of the ordered results, so a serial run stops where they first hold and later clean batches cannot undo them
shard_host.why: v4 (xreview R3, X8): with interleaved ownership a permanently broken shard leaves only every K-th batch unclean, so the global 'two consecutive' rule never fires and the attempt cap is spent on unclean batches that admit nothing. A stopped shard stops every later batch (batch k + K waits for its plan), so the stop is run-wide: STOP_HOST, report, host fix, rerun with --validation-after-host-fix as before
shard_host.fixed_before_results: set 2026-10-21 before any training collection; the 3 / 6 / 30% constants were not tuned on data

training_decision.rule: after a train stop: NO_TRAIN_RECORD_ERROR if STOP_RECORD; else NO_TRAIN_BELOW_FLOOR if A < 80; else NO_TRAIN_DISTANCE_GATE if the distance gate fails on the final admitted set; else the tiers above (TRAIN_SMALL_DATA if A < 150, TRAIN_DATA_RANGE_LIMITED if some bin < 20, TRAIN otherwise). Then validation runs for any TRAIN* decision and the validation gate may turn it into NO_TRAIN_VALIDATION_INSUFFICIENT

per_stop.STOP_TARGET: TRAIN, or TRAIN_DATA_RANGE_LIMITED when some bin is bin_limited
per_stop.STOP_CAP: tiers 1-4 on the admitted set: A >= 150 -> TRAIN / TRAIN_DATA_RANGE_LIMITED; 80 <= A < 150 -> TRAIN_SMALL_DATA; A < 80 -> NO_TRAIN_BELOW_FLOOR (back to P2, report)
per_stop.STOP_SEEDS: same as STOP_CAP (N may be < 600 because environment failures consumed seeds)
per_stop.STOP_HOST: same as STOP_CAP on the attempts so far; the run root is closed for train collection. Validation is run only by a later invocation with --validation-after-host-fix after DeepSeek reports the host fix; its own HOST_ERRORs follow the status table
per_stop.STOP_DISTANCE: NO_TRAIN_DISTANCE_GATE; stop and report, no extra collection and no post-hoc seed selection
per_stop.STOP_RECORD: NO_TRAIN_RECORD_ERROR; the recorder/judge is fixed and a NEW run root with a new prereg revision is used

training_decision.data_range_limited_label: results on TRAIN_DATA_RANGE_LIMITED (or TRAIN_SMALL_DATA with bins < 20) carry '데이터 범위 제한(구간 부족: <bin list>)' with each bin's A_b; TRAIN_SMALL_DATA results also carry '소량 데이터(A<150)'
tiers: 1. A >= 150 AND every bin A_b >= 20 -> TRAIN (normal)
2. A >= 150 AND some bin A_b < 20 -> TRAIN_DATA_RANGE_LIMITED; every result carries '데이터 범위 제한(구간 부족: <bin list>)'

3. 80 <= A < 150 -> TRAIN_SMALL_DATA; every result carries '소량 데이터(A<150)' (plus the range label if bins < 20) and interpretation is limited to the stage funnel. Rationale: with the 11/5 schedule one train+eval pass is needed to see the failing stage, and training (~4.6 GPU-h) costs less than a collection retry. Fixed before seeing any result
4. A < 80 -> NO_TRAIN_BELOW_FLOOR: no training; return to the P2 teacher carry path and report it
training_decision.owner_answer: 2026-10-21 owner answer to task 11cb2d69: interpretation (가) plus the 80 floor (tiers above)
training_decision.same_for_every_K: v4 (xreview B1, Codex H1): the decision is decision(prereg, ledger) on the final ledger; train_stop is a pure function of the results (train_closed is never read by it). For K > 1 train_closed is written only on the drained view, after which no train result arrives, so it always equals train_stop of the final data (checked: harness.pairact_collect.check_train_closed refuses a ledger where they differ). per_stop.STOP_DISTANCE therefore holds for every K

allocation.adaptive: adaptive collection: the bin of the next train attempt depends on earlier outcomes. Seeds are consumed in strict ascending order independent of the bin, so the start of a seed depends on the ledger. Yields are therefore adaptive-collection yields, not the yield of the original robot-level uniform start distribution; reports give per-bin tables and primary (8340000-199) vs extension (8340200-599) tables separately
allocation.batch_size: fixed per run root (--batch-size, default 20); recorded in the ledger header
allocation.quantity: success_b in every rule below is A_b (admitted, the same quantity as the stop rules); N_b is behavior attempts
allocation.warmup: while ANY open bin has N_b < 4: slots are round-robin over the open bins B0..B5 continuing after the last assigned bin (implementation = document)
allocation.deficit: need_b = max(0, 20 - A_b); p_b = (A_b + 1) / (N_b + 2); weight_b = need_b / max(p_b, 0.05); bin_limited bins get weight 0. Slots split by largest remainder over weight_b, ties to the lower bin index
allocation.after_minimums: when every open bin has need_b == 0 but A < 200: round-robin over the open bins
allocation.slot_order: slots are interleaved bin by bin (B0,B1,..) so a partially run batch stays balanced
allocation.deterministic: allocation reads only the ledger; identical ledger -> identical next batch

constants_rationale.warmup_4: 4 attempts per bin (24 total, about one batch) before any rate is used: the Laplace estimate (A+1)/(N+2) is then within [1/6, 5/6] and cannot zero a bin
constants_rationale.p_floor_0.05: caps one bin's weight at 20x need so a 0/k bin cannot take a whole batch; the bin_limit rule, not the floor, retires a hopeless bin
constants_rationale.laplace: (A+1)/(N+2) is the posterior mean under a uniform prior; it is defined at N = 0

sharding.scope: execution only: how batches are spread over processes and VMs. Episode judgement, the status table, the counts N/S/A/E, the stop rules, the allocation formula, bins, seed pools and their consumption order and the training decision tiers are unchanged and computed by the same functions for every K (harness.pairact_collect plan_batch / allocate / train_stop / decision). What K > 1 changes is listed in what_changes_vs_serial. Fixed before any result
sharding.K: number of shard processes = RUN_MANIFEST sharding.count, core content (fixed at FROZEN_CORE, never changed within a run root). K = 1 is the serial runner. K is chosen from the contention measurement done in measurement mode BEFORE FROZEN_CORE (RUNBOOK 1-6a); a training run root is never reopened with another K, and a host that cannot sustain K is handled as STOP_HOST (stop, report), never by re-collecting the same train seeds under a new K without a new prereg revision and an owner decision (xreview R6). D-v4-1: K <= 3 (K_max; manifest gate and CLI refuse more). Disclosed case: on the cross-review fake X7 (seed-periodic outcome success = seed % 3 == 0 or (B0/B1 and seed even), B5 always fails) serial, K = 2 and K = 3 end STOP_TARGET (A 204 / 218 / 235), K = 4 ends STOP_DISTANCE -> NO_TRAIN_DISTANCE_GATE (A 181): its lagged bin_limit closed B2 and B4 at 2/22 and 2/21 admitted, so the far band left the gate and the B2/B3 starts alone (5.7% > 0.8 m) missed the reduced 9.4%. On a non-periodic fake (per-bin rates 0.6/0.5/0.45/0.4/0.35/0) K = 2, 3 and 4 all matched the serial class (TRAIN_DATA_RANGE_LIMITED). Two VMs share the cap (e.g. gcp6 [0, 1], gcp2 [2])
sharding.owner: global batch index k is planned and run by shard k % K; each shard appends only to its own ledger run_root/shards/sII/ledger.jsonl (one process per shard: file lock; the header records shard index, K and VM)
sharding.planning_view: batch k is planned on the view = the plan rows of every batch < k plus the results of every batch <= k - K, in serial ledger order (results of batch j - K, then the plan rows of batch j). A shard waits until its view is complete. The view holds only immutable rows, so the plan of batch k does not depend on wall-clock order, VM speed or ledger sync timing (tests/test_pairact_collect_shard.py: K = 1 equals the serial ledger row for row; random schedules, threads and two run roots joined by ledger sync give the same merged ledger)
sharding.what_changes_vs_serial: for K > 1 the adaptive allocation (warmup round robin, deficit_weighted_v2 weights, bin_limit) reads counts that lag by up to K - 1 batches: in-flight batches are not counted yet. The rule is fixed in advance and never reads in-flight outcomes, but the bin sequence of a K > 1 run can differ from a serial run on the same seeds, and a bin that bin_limit would close can receive up to about (K - 1) x batch_size more attempts before its lagged count closes it (xreview R4, X7). Stop and training decision are NOT lagged: they are computed once on the drained ledger (stop) by the same functions as the serial run. Because the bin sequence can differ, the drained ledger itself (N, A, per-bin counts) can differ from a serial run on the same seeds; the rule that maps a ledger to a stop and a decision does not. Reports and the merged report state K
sharding.attempt_cap: train slots of in-flight batches are reserved against attempt_cap (room = 600 - N - reserved), so N <= 600. A planning boundary without room while batches are in flight is a batch_skipped row (no seed consumed); environment failures of the in-flight batches free room and are re-queued as in the serial run (the stop barrier waits for them, including at STOP_SEEDS)
sharding.stop: stop barrier (v4, owner 2026-10-21; xreview B1/B2, Codex H1). At a planning boundary the unchanged train_stop is evaluated on the view. (1) A stop seen while batches are in flight writes train_barrier 'hold' and no new batch is planned (batch_skipped, no seed consumed) until every in-flight batch is done; results that arrive meanwhile are kept (targets.overshoot). (2) On the drained view (no batch in flight, every result present, incl. the HOST_ERROR re-queue candidates of in-flight batches) train_stop is evaluated once more: a stop -> train_closed with that stop, fixed for the run root (no train result can arrive after it, so it equals the stop of the final data); no stop -> train_barrier 'release' and planning resumes, exactly as a serial run on that ledger would continue (e.g. a pending re-queue at STOP_SEEDS, a STOP_HOST cleared by late clean batches). (3) Validation is planned only after train_closed, never while a train batch is in flight (xreview R5). K = 1 never has batches in flight, so a stop is closed at once. STOP_HOST: train_closed is written; without --validation-after-host-fix no validation is planned and every shard returns STOP_HOST; after the host fix all shards are rerun with the flag
sharding.seeds: a seed is planned only when unconsumed (every earlier plan is in the view) or as the re-queue of a HOST_ERROR of a finished batch, so no seed is in two running batches; merge refuses a ledger set that violates this (tested with real threads)
sharding.merge: run_pairact_collect.py merge --shards K writes run_root/merged/{ledger.jsonl, report.json, merge.json}: the serial-order view of all shard ledgers. It is derived and rewritten at every merge; the shard ledgers are the originals. report / probe-cases / convert-input read --run-root run_root/merged; merge.json records every shard ledger sha256 and finished (run_end written and every planned batch done). v4: merge refuses a shard ledger that is not an append-only extension of the bytes recorded by the previous merge (merge.json shard_ledger_bytes / sha256) and a seed planned fresh twice or re-queued without an earlier environment failure in any split (check_seed_history); report on the merged root keeps the sharding block from merge.json; v5: the reader, repair_ledger and the merge seal share the committed prefix (bytes up to the last newline; an unterminated tail, even valid JSON, is uncommitted), and merge / report / convert-input refuse a completed attempt counted twice (same batch slot or same split / seed / requeue) or not matching its planned slot; convert-input refuses a sharded run root itself, a merged ledger that differs from merge.json and an unfinished merge (finished false or running batches), and refuses when any admitted world raw directory is missing on the merge VM (Codex H2/H3/H5)
sharding.vms: RUN_MANIFEST sharding.assignment maps VM -> shard indices. Two VMs exchange only the shard ledgers (rsync whole-file replace, a torn last line is ignored by the reader); the world raw directories are copied to the merge VM under the same absolute run root before convert-input. The teacher recording check is machine-bound (same_machine), so every non-primary VM runs its own recording probe and check (RUN_MANIFEST sharding.vm_recording_check, filled at FROZEN)

seeds.consumption: per split, new attempts take the next unused seed in strict ascending order regardless of bin; a HOST_ERROR re-queue reuses its own seed and bin and consumes no new seed; setup rejections and admission errors consume the seed and are never re-queued

pilot.rule: measurement mode only (recording off, candidate pairact_p2_r13): yield, bins and wall/SIM. Bin = (seed - 8343000) % 6, no adaptive allocation. Never in tensors, never pooled with A of the training run. Also the source of the 3 recording-probe starts

validation.rule: training mode only and only after train_closed / the train stop (never during or before collection, never in measurement mode, never while a train batch is in flight). Bin = index % 6, collected once each, HOST_ERROR re-queued once, not counted toward targets, cap or allocation; admitted episodes go to validation tensors. v4 (xreview B3): validation is one batch of 20, and an unclean batch admits nothing, so one HOST_ERROR world would turn into NO_TRAIN_VALIDATION_INSUFFICIENT. Every judged world of an unclean validation batch is therefore re-queued once with the same seed and bin like an environment failure (category environment, outcome unclean_batch_requeue, its judged outcome kept in the row, not in N); if the re-queued run's batch is unclean again the seed is judged but not admitted (success_not_admitted:batch_not_clean), with no further re-queue. The gate (>= 8 of 20) is unchanged

seeds.overlap_check: pilot, train, validation and heldout are pairwise disjoint and disjoint from seeds.json known_ranges (harness.pairact_collect.check_seed_ranges at load; scripts/check_pairact_r1_seeds.py --scan-refs for git refs, output saved as seed-check.json in the run root)

validation_gate.rule: after validation: admitted validation pairs >= 8 of 20 AND the union of sidecar stages over admitted validation episodes contains approach, alignment, ready, execute, carry, place, complete. Otherwise NO_TRAIN_VALIDATION_INSUFFICIENT: stop and report; no extra validation seeds, no replacement, no relaxing
validation_gate.rationale: OFFLINE_GATE G4 needs every registered transition present in validation and fails otherwise; 8 pairs = 16 robot streams give >= 16 instances per transition so the 0.80 recall threshold is resolved at 1/16; the required stages are the RUNBOOK section 2 missing_stages list (recover may be absent)
validation_gate.report: validation S/20 and A/20 with environment failures listed separately

dart_noise.mechanism: existing teacher --noise (result.noise = 'DART-inspired_fixed_pilot'): 5% of grasp-segment steps outside done/complete/ready apply a perturbed command; the label keeps clean_teacher_command and perturbed=true. Carry segment rows are never perturbed
dart_noise.when_on: a separate run root and ledger tag noise=on; every attempt records perturbed_rows / total_rows per robot; reports never pool noise-on and noise-off
dart_noise.trigger_candidate: only if recover-stage rows in admitted successes are < 5% of rows after collection; needs Claude approval and a new prereg revision
dart_noise.gpu_status: noise is off for every candidate: adapter -a-c2 aaabddb1 scripts/run_beampair1.py:453 builds run_kwargs=dict(record_training=False, noise=False, ...) at its single runner.run call site and pairact_p3_collect only adds the recording keys (checked 2026-10-21 Oracle); re-checked on the -a-c3 pin before FROZEN_CORE (RUNBOOK 1-0)

bias_report.ks: two-sample KS (asymptotic p) on PAIR-level values (mean of the two robots' start distance; mean |yaw offset|) between the three groups physical_failure, success_not_admitted, admitted (three pairwise comparisons); one value per pair episode because both robots share the bin. Informational, not a gate; conditional on the adaptive allocation
bias_report.per_bin_table: bin, N, S, A, S/N, A/N, need, environment failures by kind, setup rejections, bin_limited, failure sub-reasons; also split primary vs extension seeds
bias_report.recover_count: rows with teacher_phase mapped to stage recover in admitted episodes (sidecar)

distance_gate.applies_to: robot-level start distances of ADMITTED train pair episodes (both robots of every admitted pair)
distance_gate.rule: all 0.1 m bins of [0.3, 1.2] occupied AND share of distances > 0.8 m >= 25%, both on the distance range that is not excluded (range_excluded below)
distance_gate.when: STOP_DISTANCE: at every batch boundary once A >= 150 and every far bin (B4, B5) has A_b >= 20 or is bin_limited (D-v4-1; before that the gate is reported but is not a stop reason); and on the final admitted set after any train stop (training_decision). For K > 1 the stop is only fixed on the drained view (sharding.stop)
distance_gate.on_failure: stop and report; no post-hoc seed selection, no extra collection, no relaxing
distance_gate.rationale: uniform 0.3-1.2 m gives 44% above 0.8 m; 25% (57% of uniform) keeps the beamact4 failure mode (TRAIN 0.09% above 0.8 m) out. v3s claimed this also allowed the far bins to be bin_limited, but with B4 and B5 both limited only B2/B3 can reach > 0.8 m (about 1/3 of their starts, ~16% of all), so the gate was effectively NO_TRAIN_DISTANCE_GATE (xreview X5). v4 keeps 57% of the uniform share of the open range instead and labels the reduced range
distance_gate.range_excluded: v4 (xreview R2, owner (ii)): a distance band (bins.distance_edges_m interval) whose bins are ALL bin_limited (e.g. B4 and B5 = 0.9-1.2 m) leaves the gate: the admitted robot starts of its bins leave the denominator, its 0.1 m cells leave the occupancy check, and the required share above 0.8 m is scaled to the remaining range: required = 0.25 x u_open / u_full, u = uniform share of (0.8, 1.2] in the range (B4+B5 excluded: 0.25 x (0.1/0.6) / (0.4/0.9) = 0.094; nothing excluded: 0.25). Every result carries '거리 관문 축소(제한 구간 제외: <bands>, 요구 비율 <x>)' (decision.labels, report distance_gate.label). A band with one open bin is not excluded
distance_gate.required_share_formula: required share above 0.8 m = 0.25 x u_open / u_full, u = uniform share of (0.8, 1.2] in a range: u_full = 0.4 / 0.9 (0.3-1.2 m), u_open = the same over the distance bands that are not excluded. Example: B4 and B5 both bin_limited -> 0.9-1.2 m excluded, u_open = 0.1 / 0.6, required = 0.25 x (0.1/0.6) / (0.4/0.9) = 0.094. Nothing excluded -> 0.25. Approved by the owner (D-v4-2): it carries the original intent (25% = 57% of the uniform share) to the remaining range

audit_outputs.ledger: every attempt (behavior or environment), every setup rejection (generator budget exhaustion included), bin_limited rows and batch_done rows with status, HOST_ERROR, exit code, rejection_table absolute path, artifact manifest sha256
audit_outputs.setup_rejection_row: seed, bin, split (slot values; the generator audit must agree), requeue flag, gate funnel (per gate cumulative passed / rejected), blocked objects by name with counts (static obstacle id, cargo item id, bounds, beam_1, peer_robot, the runtime certified-stance blocker per rejected end), minimum gap (m) per gate or not_measured, generator source sha and file sha256, reproduce command with absolute paths (collect_cases.py --slot-json ... --stdout). A rejected re-queued slot leaves the re-queue (never re-queued)
audit_outputs.case_plan: every accepted case carries the same generator audit (gate funnel, blockers, min gaps, reproduce)
audit_outputs.episode_command: the --episode-cmd template must contain --rejection-table <absolute path> and --cap-s; template sha256, the input rejection table path and cap are in the ledger header
audit_outputs.batch_rejection_table: summary.rejection_table must be an absolute path to an existing file for a clean batch
audit_outputs.launch_binding: teacher 산출물마다 <out>.pairact-binding.json: manifest gate core, episode template/argv sha256, cwd, episode pin(pre)과 pin_post, stack(pre)과 stack_post. pin = wrapper 절대경로·sha256, python 경로·realpath·sha256, WARP_SOURCE_ROOT realpath, cwd; stack = teacher·adapter·root의 realpath·HEAD·tracked-change flag. check-rows와 convert-input은 pin·stack 불일치, pin_post/stack_post 없음, v8 이전 형식을 거부한다

reporting.A: 교사 시연 수집(적응형 구간 배정, pair episode 단위): 물리 성공 S / 시도 N, 최종 채택 A / 시도 N (데이터 필터용, 학습 결과 아님). 200은 채택 목표이고 분모가 아님 + 구간별 표 + 환경 실패 별도
reporting.pilot: pilot 수율 측정: 물리 성공 S / 시도 N (수율 측정, 시연 아님; seed 8343000-039). The READY_FOR_REVIEW pilot 26/40 (STATUS 2026-10-21) ran on the -c4 stack, not the pinned -c5 stack: it is never used as the yield basis of -c5 collection (the 33% yield behind the 600 cap is decision-doc 3, not the pilot), and reports name purpose and stack (pilot_yield_only -c4 vs probe_source -c5)
reporting.validation: validation: 물리 성공 S / 20, 채택 A / 20 (환경 실패 별도)
reporting.B: 교사 관문 n/40 (교사 신뢰도, 학습 결과 아님). Separate run; never computed from collection attempts

owner_decisions_v4.D-v4-1: 2026-10-21, before freeze (not a post-hoc change: nothing is frozen and no training collection exists). STOP_DISTANCE is evaluated only once every far bin (the bins of the farthest distance band, B4 and B5) has A_b >= min_admitted_per_bin (20) or is bin_limited; before that the distance gate is not a stop reason. Reason: the gate checks that the admitted start distribution reaches the far range; evaluated while the far bins are still being collected, its outcome depends on the execution (K). The distance gate on the final admitted set (training_decision) is unchanged. Follow-up rule set by the owner in the same decision: if K = 4 still gives another decision class than the serial run on the cross-review fakes, the case is disclosed and K is capped at 3 -> it did (sharding.K_max)
